episodes.213533: During a long duration heatwave a weak upper level disturbance touched off more numerous storms than previous days.
episodes.213552: A slow-moving cold front sparked spotty severe thunderstorms.
episodes.213620: The stationary front that caused numerous instances of severe thunderstorms and flash flooding on July 5th continues to linger over central Pennsylvania into July 6, 2026. The environment over central Pennsylvania did possess slightly less instability and shear compared to previous days; however, sufficient instability within a moist environment and a lifting mechanism allowed for some scattered showers and storms to develop during the late afternoon hours. These storms mainly formed across northwestern Pennsylvania, where multiple rounds of locally heavy rainfall caused flash flooding in McKean and Elk Counties before shifting further southward as showers and storms congealed into a line with the bulk of severe activity shifting towards western Pennsylvania. Heavy rainfall still caused multiple instances of flash flooding in Clearfield County as well before shifting further south into Centre and Blair Counties and resulting in multiple instances of flash flooding during the evening hours. The most considerable flooding happened further northeast, in the village of Potter Brook, Tioga County, where multiple homes were evacuated due to water up to the first floor and multiple roadways were impassable.
episodes.213622: A weak shortwave neared the Upstate of SC early in the day with surface troughing already evident into the Midlands of SC by the mid morning. Surface dewpoints were in the mid 70s much of the day, with MLCAPE values up to 2500-3000 J/kg developing by the late morning. This lead to a cluster of severe thunderstorms over Lexington and Richland Counties during the late morning that brought scattered tree damage, including a likely microburst near the Forest Acres neighborhood in Columbia. Efficient rainfall also brought an isolated instance of flash flooding in Lexington County. Recovery ensued the remainder of the day with another round of thunderstorms bringing damaging wind gusts during the evening across the southeastern Midlands into the Pee Dee. The evening thunderstorms also brought a copious amount of lightning with the Newberry County Sheriff reporting that the EOC building was struck by lightning, causing communications to go down.
episodes.213680: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of July 7, 2026. These thunderstorms produced heavy rain, causing flooding across portions of Lawrence and Williamson counties.
episodes.213735: A slow moving boundary resulted in showers and thunderstorms that produced a localized two to four inches of rain.
episodes.213736: A stationary thunderstorm produced two to four inches of rain across western Augusta County.  This resulted in an isolated instance of flash flooding.
episodes.213755: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked southward across Traverse and Big Stone counties on the afternoon of July 6. A weak tornado touched down over agricultural land in northwestern Traverse County approximately 10 miles west of Tintah, causing no structural damage. In Big Stone County, the storms produced consecutive wind gusts of 60 mph near Lismore Colony.
episodes.213769: Slow moving thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced localized rainfall totals of two to four inches. The maximum over Prince William, Fauquier, and Loudoun counties was upwards of six inches. Some thunderstorms trained over one another, resulting in an isolated instance of flash flooding.
episodes.213786: Hail and strong thunderstorm winds were observed in the Watertown area late in the evening of July 6th. A 58 mph wind gust was recorded on a personal weather station 2 miles northwest of Watertown, while quarter sized hail was observed by the public 4 miles west of Kranzburg.
episodes.213787: Strong thunderstorm winds were observed over parts of northeast South Dakota during the late morning hours of July 7th. A peak wind gust of 74 mph was recorded on a personal weather station 6 miles west of Barnard (Brown county), while a 60 mph wind gust was recorded on the South Dakota State University mesonet station in Leola.
episodes.214193: A southward moving cold front produced a cluster of thunderstorms during the evening hours. One storm became severe and produced some wind damage.
episodes.214294: Monsoon showers and storms formed during the afternoon.  One produced a brief landspout tornado.
episodes.214295: High based showers formed across the area, producing some strong outflow winds gusts.
episodes.214667: A weak shortwave moving across Wyoming produced multiple thunderstorms, resulting in numerous landspout sightings in Laramie County.
episodes.214668: A weak shortwave moving across Wyoming produced multiple thunderstorms, resulting in strong winds across the Nebraska panhandle.
episodes.214689: A surface low pressure system stalled over Arkansas for a couple days and an attendant boundary consisted of a stationary boundary that eventually became a warm front and lifted northward. However over this period of time, damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding would be noted across much of the state.
episodes.214844: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.214944: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.214947: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.215424: An isolated thunderstorm developed in the early evening hours along the southeast Georgia coast. The storm became strong enough to produce an isolated instance of wind damage in McIntosh County.
episodes.215487: A stalled frontal boundary across Wyoming and a shortwave moving through brought another day of strong to severe thunderstorms to portions of central Wyoming. Wind gusts over 58 mph were reported in Sweetwater, Natrona, Fremont, Sublette, and Johnson Counties. The strongest wind gust reported was 64 mph at Twenty Mile Hill to the north of Casper in Natrona County.
episodes.215512: Another shortwave crossed the area and brought more thunderstorms with strong wind gusts. Locations along Interstate 80 in far eastern Sweetwater County and along Interstate 90 in eastern Johnson County recorded wind gusts of 58 mph.
episodes.215624: A weak midlevel weather system paired with bountiful moisture helped fire numerous scattered showers and thunderstorms. A couple of storms produced heavy rainfall and strong to severe winds in isolated locations.
episodes.215849: Strong to severe storms were more prevalent across northwestern Minnesota on July 6th, but a few stronger storms did move into the Brainerd Lakes area during the afternoon and evening hours. Most of the hail from these storms was below severe limits, but gusty winds led to reports of downed trees in the area.
episodes.216049: Scattered to numerous showers and storms developed in the afternoon through late evening hours across central North Carolina. Numerous damaging wind reports were observed, as well as a few isolated reports of flash flooding.
episodes.216050: A cold front over the southern Middle Atlantic states dropped into central North Carolina during the evening hours. Scattered showers and storms led to damaging winds and flash flooding across the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain.
episodes.216064: A severe thunderstorm outflow wind gust occurred at the Pocatello Regional Airport ASOS.
episodes.216066: Thunderstorms developed over the Pine Ridge of northern Sheridan County during the afternoon hours of July 6th. This activity initiated in the vicinity of a surface trough. As it moved east into better low level moisture, storms became severe over northeastern Sheridan County. Other severe storms tracked through Garden County producing a wind gust to 60 MPH. Elsewhere, 60 MPH winds were reported in Keya Paha County with wind damage to trees reported south of Clinton in Sheridan County.
episodes.216075: A line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours across the western Nebraska Panhandle on July 7th. As this activity pushed east into the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle, it produced quarter sized hail in far northern Sheridan County. Storms then weakened as the tracked east into Cherry County.
episodes.216192: Over the course of several days between July 6th and July 9th, an unsettled pattern persisted across the Ohio and Tennessee Valley as a cutoff low meandered across the region. A humid, unstable environment was present throughout this time period with dew point temperatures in the mid 70s and precipitable water values near or exceeding 2 inches. On top of this, relatively weak steering flow in the mid-levels of the atmosphere lead to slow movement of showers and thunderstorms which developed, resulting in localized heavy rainfall amounts and flash flooding. Scattered flash flooding occurred across central Kentucky over the four day period, with severe weather impacts mainly being limited to isolated downbursts from hydrometeor loading in otherwise disorganized cells. However, by the 9th, the ingestion of the cutoff low into broader troughing did provide for slightly stronger wind shear and better storm organization. With a seasonably humid and unstable environment remaining in place, this stronger wind shear did promote a bit more coverage of strong to severe storms, with a couple wind damage reports and a spin-up tornado being observed during the evening and early nighttime hours on July 9th.
episodes.216221: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across mainly East Tennessee on the 7th. These began developing during the late morning hours and continued into the late evening hours before dissipating, producing a few instances of flash flooding.
episodes.216344: A severe thunderstorm occurred near Bowman in Bowman County early in the morning along a frontal boundary and in an environment with moderate shear but weak instability. There was a collapsed barn roof northwest of the Bowman Airport due to the damaging thunderstorm wind gusts. Radar suggests the strong winds were associated with the collapse of a thunderstorm updraft over the impacted location. The nearby Bowman NDAWN station reported wind gusts up to 76 mph.
episodes.216441: A line of thunderstorms tracked southeast across central MN during the evening on Monday, July 6th. The storms generally weakened as they moved southeast, however, several reports of wind damage were recorded across central MN before the storms weakened. The majority of the reported wind damage was downed or uprooted trees and tree limbs.
episodes.216445: There were a few reports of severe weather on July 7th as scattered storms moved through MN in the afternoon and late evening. More widespread storms moved through very late on the 7th and into the early morning of the 8th, but the severe weather environment had weakened by the time they moved through.
episodes.216533: Active weather was observed on a daily basis in West Virginia from July 6th to the 9th amid hot temperatures and ample moisture. Showers and strong thunderstorms fired up quickly each afternoon, filled with heavy downpours and damaging wind gusts. Downed trees and power lines were the main impacts with severe weather during this stretch of time, along with street flooding and creeks rising out of their banks. The active weather pattern stretched further into the month due to an encroaching frontal boundary that stalled over the region. Daily showers and storms then continued over West Virginia heading into the middle of the month.
episodes.216535: Slow moving showers and thunderstorms produced by strong daytime heating on July 6th casted areas of severe weather and flash flooding to the Central Appalachians. In southwest Virginia, flash flooding was observed in Buchanan County due to the heavy downpours caused by the slow movement of activity. Local roads in the county were closed as a result of the high water for a period of time during that afternoon. Strongly motivated by daytime heating, these storms quickly came to an end around sunset and concluded the risk of flash flooding for the day.
episodes.216596: Strong thunderstorms developed across southeast Mississippi and produced high winds.
episodes.216597: Thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.216609: A weakness in the ridge aloft and the presence of a remnant outflow boundary (a result of decaying convection across Oklahoma) led to scattered thunderstorms during the afternoons of July 5th and 6th. Damaging wind gusts were the most common severe weather occurrence, especially at Olney Municipal Airport in Young County where millions of dollars of damage occurred, though a few reports of large hail were also received.
episodes.216713: A slow-moving upper level trough extended from central Arkansas through the Lower Mississippi Valley at midday on July 7, 2026. Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along and east of the trough axis, across the Mid-South, during the afternoon. Deep layer shear around 25 knots and MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg supported a severe storm over eastern Arkansas which produced wind damage.
episodes.216754: Daytime heating destabilized the humid air mass in place across southeast Louisiana during the afternoon of July 7, allowing scattered thunderstorms to develop along local mesoscale boundaries. One strong thunderstorm near Prairieville produced damaging winds that downed several trees shortly. Farther east, additional thunderstorms developed across the New Orleans metropolitan area late in the afternoon and produced locally intense rainfall with flash flooding.
episodes.216755: A typical midsummer pattern prevailed across the northern Gulf Coast during the early morning hours of July 7, with weak large-scale forcing and scattered convection favored over the marine areas during the overnight and morning hours. Thunderstorms developed over southern Lake Pontchartrain shortly after midnight, where localized convective downdrafts produced strong wind gusts near the New Orleans Lakefront.
episodes.216768: Instability remained pooled near a boundary from south central South Dakota into southern Minnesota. With the tail end of a weak mid-level disturbance brushing past the area overnight, isolated storms developed and produced spotty damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216770: Instability remained pooled near a boundary from south central South Dakota into southern Minnesota. With the tail end of a weak mid-level disturbance brushing past the area overnight, slow-moving isolated storms developed, which allowed hail to fall for an extended period.
episodes.216829: The continued presence of a weak upper level disturbance that lingered across East Texas and North Louisiana on July 6th again focused adequate large scale ascent within a hot, moist, and unstable air mass for scattered severe thunderstorms to develop across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana during the mid and late afternoon hours. These storms produced damaging winds which downed trees and power lines, as well as isolated instances of large hail, before diminishing during the evening.
episodes.216835: The continued presence of a weak upper level disturbance that lingered across East Texas and North Louisiana on July 6th again focused adequate large scale ascent within a hot, moist, and unstable air mass for scattered severe thunderstorms to develop across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana during the mid and late afternoon hours. These storms produced damaging winds which downed trees and power lines, as well as isolated instances of large hail, before diminishing during the evening.
episodes.216864: An unusually strong and deep upper level disturbance lingered across the Mid-South and into Southwest Arkansas, Northwest Louisiana, and East Texas during the early morning hours of July 7th, as it remained wedged in between two upper level ridges over the Southern Rockies into the western sections of the Southern Plains, and over the Eastern Seaboard and Southeast United States. This trough had focused numerous severe thunderstorms across the region on July 6th, and while the intensity of these storms diminished with the loss of daytime heating and resultant instability, multiple outflow boundaries from these storms, coupled with ample moisture, and large scale forcing along the upper trough itself continued to focus renewed shower and thunderstorm development even during the overnight/early morning hours on the 7th across the region. One isolated severe thunderstorm was able to develop over Northern Caddo Parish in the community of Belcher, where a tree was blown down over a roadway.
episodes.216865: An unusually strong and deep upper level disturbance lingered across the Mid-South and into Southwest Arkansas, Northwest Louisiana, and East Texas during the early morning hours of July 7th, as it remained wedged in between two upper level ridges over the Southern Rockies into the western sections of the Southern Plains, and over the Eastern Seaboard and Southeast United States. This trough had focused numerous severe thunderstorms across the region on July 6th, with multiple outflow boundaries from these storms, coupled with ample moisture, large scale forcing along the upper trough itself, and renewed daytime heating which yielded strong instability, focusing shower and thunderstorm development during the morning and afternoon hours on the 7th across East Texas and North Louisiana. Some of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds that downed trees, an isolated instance of large hail, as well as heavy rainfall that led to localized flash flooding in Smith County throughout the cities of Tyler and Lindale, before diminishing late in the day.
episodes.216866: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the Big Country and Concho Valley. Some of the storms were severe and mainly produced wind damage.
episodes.216894: A weak upper trough sat over southwest Louisiana for multiple days. This allowed scattered diurnal storms to develop with a couple storms becoming severe.
episodes.216935: A broad upper trough and weak surface low combined with strong heating to result in scattered thunderstorm development with locally heavy rain across eastern Virginia.
episodes.216958: Two storms ended up causing some low end severe weather in Fall River county.
episodes.216988: A slow moving line of showers and thunderstorms produced efficient rainfall for flash flooding across portions of western Pennsylvania on the 6th. PWAT values were just above the 90th percentile in the morning sounding at 1.82 inches supporting the heavy rainfall rates. A couple of the areas most impacted by flash flooding include Dixonville in Indiana county, where 25 homes had basement flooding and in Dawson in Fayette county where the first floor and basements of some homes were flooded and damage occurred to several private bridges.
episodes.217001: Supercells and a QLCS thunderstorm complex developed during the afternoon and evening hours resulting in multiple reports of large hail and widespread damaging winds. A weak tornado developed in Kittson County, while a strong  tornado developed with the QLCS complex in Becker County. EF-2 damage occurred at Floyd Lake north of Detroit Lakes, MN with that tornado.
episodes.217180: A waterspout was observed in association with a convective shower embedded within weak east-southeast lower tropospheric flow.  Weak low-level ridging extended across the western North Atlantic and south Florida.
episodes.217256: A storm passed over musselshell county, producing hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.217397: An isolated strong to severe storm caused wind damage in Hinds County shortly after midnight.

The tornado appears to have begun about northwest of Wheeler Lake, tracking over the lake where it caused roof damage to a few homes and snapped the trunks of a few large oak and poplar trees on the west side of the lake. The tornado continued east where it appears to have widened to around a half mile in width along the western shore of (Big) Floyd Lake. This is where the highest rated survey damage occurred with a few anchored and modestly built garages were collapsed. A few other more questionably built garages and outbuildings were swept clean in the Oakland Beach neighborhood along with widespread roofing and tree damage. It was in this same area that a 6 by 12 foot horse trailer was lofted and carried about 1/8sm from its stables. The tornado then continued across the lake onto the eastern shore inflicting more roof and tree damage. The last visible surveyed damage was near the corner of Co HWY 25 and Anchor Rd about 3 miles east of the southern end of (Big) Floyd Lake. Based on Satellite the tornado appears to have tracked another 3 miles ESE from where it crossed Co HWY 25. Max wind speed estimated at 115 mph. ||1 injury can be directly attributed to the tornado as a homeowner was injured in their home when their roof was removed by the tornado. The second injury was after the tornado during the cleanup stage and could due to shock or trauma according to the|county emergency manager. The details and circumstances of the third injury are unknown as the individual was not transported by EMS.

Heavy rain caused flooding in the Lawrenceburg area. Geri Street was covered with water. Some water made it into the front door of a restaurant on the corner of Geri Street and Business Avenue. A driveway to a residence off of Buffalo Road near David Street was also washed out. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain caused the parking lot of the Brentwood YMCA along with cars in the parking lot to become flooded, likely as the nearby creek overfilled its banks. Damages are a rough estimate.
Hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter reported.
Local news showed the ground floor apartments at the end of Ida Street were inundated with flood waters.
A tree was reported down over Pats Branch Drive.
Hail up to an inch in diameter reported.
Several reports of flooding were received, centralized around the Interstate 540 and  Chapel Hill Road intersection.
